pageCache.text:
Soaring with Compassion
Hope, Respect, Wisdom
Beechcroft St Paul's
It is my pleasure to welcome you to our school website, which I hope gives you a flavour of the compassionate and ambitious school we are. We are passionate about nurturing hearts that dream, minds that grow and a community that walks together in kindness and understanding as we live out our Christian values of hope, respect and wisdom. Please do come and see us in action - we would love to welcome you.
Useful Links
Latest News
Year 2 rounded off their Science learning on habitats by creating their own bug hotels in our gardening area. Before getting hands-on, they recapped everything they had learned about what living things need to survive and explored how different habitats support different minibeasts. There was some fantastic teamwork, creativity and scientific thinking on display as the children designed and built their microhabitats. Well done, Year 2!
What an incredible day at Beechfest! A huge thank you to everyone who came along and helped make this year's school fete such a fantastic success. We were absolutely delighted to see so many families, friends and members of our community enjoying the day. The amazing turnout and wonderful atmosphere made it a truly special event. A very special thank you goes to our fantastic PTFA and Mrs Conroy, who worked tirelessly behind the scenes to organise such a brilliant event. Their hard work, dedication and enthusiasm made Beechfest possible, and we are so grateful for everything they did. And, of course, we can't forget one of the biggest moments of the day... Miss Hawker was the one who got slimed! Thank you for being such a great sport and helping to make the day even more memorable. Thank you once again to everyone who attended, volunteered, donated, supported and helped create such a wonderful community event. We can't wait to do it all again next year!
Don't forgetit's Beechfest tomorrow after school! Who will get slimed? We can't wait to see you all there!
Our Year 4s are having an amazing time on their residential at the Ancient Technology Centre! They've been dressing up in historical clothing, making their own food, and stepping back in time to experience life as our ancestors did. What a fantastic adventure and a brilliant way to bring history to life!
Our Year 1 children had a fantastic day at Monkey World recently! They loved seeing the amazing primates, learning about conservation, and enjoying time in the adventure play parks. It was a wonderful day of learning, exploration, and fun. We are so proud of how well they represented our school!
What a fantastic KS2 Colour War Sports Day! We were treated to beautiful sunshine and an even more beautiful display of teamwork, determination and encouragement from our amazing pupils. It was wonderful to see the children cheering each other on, celebrating each other's successes and giving every event their very best effort. There were lots of smiles, plenty of fun and some fantastic sporting performances throughout the day. A huge well done to all of our KS2 children for taking part with such enthusiasm, and thank you to everyone who came along to support them and help make the day so special!
Join us next Friday for our fantastic Beechfest Summer Fayre – packed with fun, games, treats and plenty of summer smiles! Who will get GUNGED? Three brave members of staff have volunteered to take the plunge! Vote for your favourite by donating £1 per vote – and there's no limit, so vote as many times as you like!
What a fantastic day Year 2 had exploring the magnificent Corfe Castle! From climbing the ancient ruins to uncovering fascinating facts, our young historians loved every minute of their adventure. The children were full of curiosity, smiles, and excellent behaviour throughout the day. We are so proud of them all! What a castle-tastic trip!
What an incredible Year 6 residential at PGL! Despite the soaring temperatures, our children were absolutely amazing from start to finish. They showed resilience, determination, teamwork, and enthusiasm in every activity, embracing every challenge with smiles on their faces. We are so proud of the way they supported one another, stepped outside their comfort zones, and represented our school so brilliantly. They have created memories and friendships that will last a lifetime. A huge thank you to the staff who made the trip possible and ensured everyone stayed safe and had a fantastic time in the heat. Well done, Year 6you were outstanding!
With the current Red Heat Alert and warmer weather, this is a friendly reminder about staying safe around the coast and open water. Please see the poster for some important water safety advice.
To help everyone stay comfortable in the heat, we've been making the most of our air-conditioned classrooms, opening classrooms at lunchtime, and running our indoor quiet lunch club. KS1 also enjoyed an earlier lunch to avoid the hottest part of the day. There's been plenty of shade-seeking, water play, and water-drinking throughout the day too! A big thank you to our PTFA for the ice pops (and lollies for staff!) delivered today – they went down a treat!

pageCache.pageTitle: Beechcroft St Paul's C of E Primary School - Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
At Beechcroft St Paul’s Primary School, the Primary PE and Sport Premium is used strategically to enhance the quality and breadth of our physical education, ensuring all pupils benefit from enriched sporting experiences and develop lifelong healthy habits.
Our vision is to provide every child with access to both competitive sport and enjoyable physical activity from the moment they join us in Reception through to Year 6. Funding supports high-quality equipment for gross motor skill development in the Early Years, enabling strong physical foundations to be built from the outset.
The grant also strengthens leadership and competitive opportunities. Our PE Lead, Mr Fuhrmann, serves as Chairperson of the Weymouth & Portland Primary Sports Leader Group, ensuring pupils have access to up to 40 sporting events across the academic year. Through Sport Premium funding, children are able to participate in a wide range of competitions and festivals, increasing engagement, confidence and school representation within the local community.
We use the grant to broaden pupils’ experiences beyond the National Curriculum, providing access to activities such as windsurfing, sailing, climbing and archery. These opportunities expose children to the extensive sporting provision available within our coastal locality and encourage sustained participation beyond primary school.
Recognising our unique coastal context, a significant priority of our Sport Premium spending is swimming and water safety. From Year 3 to Year 6, all pupils attend a block of swimming lessons annually. This sustained investment ensures increasing numbers of pupils meet and exceed national swimming expectations, equipping them with essential life skills and promoting safety in and around water.
Through careful and purposeful use of the Sport Premium, we ensure improved participation, increased confidence, enhanced staff expertise and measurable progress in swimming competency — ultimately supporting pupils to lead safe, active and healthy lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Beechcroft St Paul's C of E Primary School - Enrichment
pageCache.text:
Enrichment
Enrichment at Beechcroft
At Beechcroft, enrichment is a vital part of how we Soar with Compassion. Our wide-ranging enrichment offer brings learning to life, nurturing the whole child and supporting our core values of hope, respect and wisdom.
Through enrichment activities, children are encouraged to explore new interests, develop talents, and build confidence beyond the classroom. These experiences help broaden horizons, allowing children to discover what they enjoy and what they can achieve. By engaging with clubs, visits, visitors and special events, pupils deepen their understanding of their place in the world, learning to appreciate diversity, community and the impact of their actions on others.
Enrichment also provides meaningful opportunities for children to practise making responsible decisions—working collaboratively, showing respect, taking risks, and demonstrating perseverance. Guided by our values, children learn to act with kindness, reflect thoughtfully, and grow in wisdom as they navigate new challenges.
Our enrichment programme ensures every child has the opportunity to thrive, dream big and develop the skills, character and compassion needed to soar—now and in the future.
Our enrichment programme plays a key role in promoting Fundamental British Values and preparing children to be responsible, active citizens. Through a wide range of enrichment opportunities, children experience and develop:
Democracy – by sharing ideas, taking part in group decision-making, pupil voice activities and collaborative projects.
The Rule of Law – through understanding expectations, following agreed rules, and recognising the importance of fairness and responsibility.
Individual Liberty – by making choices, exploring personal interests, and developing confidence to express themselves safely and respectfully.
Mutual Respect – by showing kindness, valuing others, and treating everyone with consideration and care.
Tolerance of Other Faiths and Beliefs – by learning alongside others, celebrating diversity, and developing empathy for different beliefs, cultures and experiences.
By embedding these values within our enrichment offer, we ensure children not only broaden their horizons but also grow into thoughtful, respectful and compassionate members of society—ready to soar with confidence and purpose.

pageCache.pageTitle: Beechcroft St Paul's C of E Primary School - SEND
pageCache.text:
SEND
At Beechcroft St Paul’s Primary School, we are committed to delivering a high-quality, inclusive curriculum that meets the needs of all learners, including children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). We believe every child should have access to a rich, engaging and meaningful education that supports their individual strengths and needs.
Our approach to SEND is embedded across the whole curriculum. Through adaptive teaching, personalised support and carefully chosen resources, we ensure that all children are able to access learning, make progress and feel valued in every subject. By creating an inclusive environment where differences are recognised and celebrated, we support our curriculum drivers of Broadening Our Horizons, Understanding Our Place in the World, and Becoming Responsible Decision Makers.
Broadening Our Horizons
We are committed to ensuring that children with SEND have full access to the experiences and opportunities offered across the curriculum. Teachers use adaptive teaching strategies, flexible resources and personalised support so that every child can engage meaningfully with their learning.
Our dedicated team, led by our Inclusion Lead, works closely with families and external specialists to provide targeted support where needed. In addition, children benefit from nurturing spaces such as The Nest, which provides a calm and supportive environment to help develop confidence, social skills and emotional wellbeing. These approaches help children feel secure, valued and ready to explore new ideas and experiences.
Understanding Our Place in the World
We are passionate about helping children with SEND develop a strong sense of identity and belonging. Through an inclusive curriculum and supportive classroom environment, children are encouraged to recognise their strengths, express their ideas and understand the value they bring to their community.
Learning experiences help children explore important values such as respect, belonging and responsibility. With support from trusted adults and nurturing spaces such as The Nest, children are encouraged to build confidence, ask questions and understand their role within the school community and the wider world.
Becoming Responsible Decision Makers
Supporting children to make positive and responsible choices is an important part of our SEND provision. Teachers and support staff help children understand choices, consequences and how to manage emotions in different situations.
Through supportive relationships and structured guidance, children develop skills such as emotional regulation, independence and problem solving. Our trained ELSAs (Emotional Literacy Support Assistants) provide additional support where needed, helping children build self-awareness and resilience.
These approaches help children grow in confidence and independence, supporting them to make thoughtful decisions and participate positively in school life.

Wraparound Care
Welcome to Wraparound Care
We offer wraparound care for children in Eden (nursery) through to Year 6 who attend Beechcroft St. Paul's Primary School.
The breakfast club session in the morning runs from 7:45am - 8:40am; the after-school session runs from the end of the school day until 5.45pm and aims to offer a friendly, nurturing space for children to be after-school.
4:10 – 5:45 £7.50 (For those attending a sports club from 3:10-4:10)
At wraparound care, we understand the importance of a relaxed environment where children can choose their own activities both inside and outside, mixing with different aged children in a fun and stimulating environment. You’ll find us located in the school hall in the mornings and our brand new library after school.
We have a booking system that enables you flexibility to accommodate your needs of wrap around care.
All sessions will need to be booked and paid for via the Arbor App.
Sessions will be charged as follows and must be booked at least 24 hours in advance on Arbor:
4:10 – 5:45 £7.50 (For those attending a sports club from 3:10-4:10)
Late collection from the after-school club (past 5.45pm) will result in a late collection fee being charged at £7.00 per half an hour.

Governance
The governors of Beechcroft St Paul’s are a group of people from the local community who have come together to support and challenge the headteacher and the staff to ensure that the school provides the best learning opportunities for all its pupils . Parent and Staff governors are elected to represent those groups within the school.
Chair of Governors - Mrs J Moore - office@beechcroft.dsat.org.uk
A copy of governors’ meeting minutes can be made available by request from the clerk via: truffle@dsat.org.uk
Please note charges may apply, more information can be found in the DSAT Publication Scheme.
DSAT Scheme of Delegation: Click Here
On 1 August 2017 Beechcroft St Paul’s joined the Diocese of Salisbury Academy Trust and all the governors have been reappointed by DSAT. Foundation Governors have been nominated by St Paul’s Church and ratified by the Salisbury Diocesan Board of Education.
We take part in training sessions to keep up to date with changes in schools and education so that we can be more effective governors. We come into school to work with the headteacher, the staff and pupils so we know how much progress the children are making in comparison with schools nationally. It’s a joy and a privilege to serve our community in this way. The governors meet together twice a term and attend other meetings too.

Curriculum
Our Curriculum
At Beechcroft St Paul’s, we believe every child and adult should thrive—personally, spiritually, and academically. Rooted in our vision, Soaring with Compassion, and inspired by St Paul’s words in Philippians, our curriculum is shaped by the Christian values of hope, respect, and wisdom.
We are committed to providing a purposeful and empowering curriculum that prepares every child for the next stage of their education and opens doors to the wider world. Core literacy and numeracy skills are central to all that we do, forming the strong foundations upon which broader learning is built. Our curriculum is designed to spark curiosity, inspire ambition and nurture a lifelong love of learning.
Our curriculum is shaped by our key drivers: Broadening Our Horizons, Understanding Our Place in the World, and Becoming Responsible Decision Makers. Through carefully planned experiences, enrichment opportunities and meaningful learning, we encourage children to look beyond their immediate surroundings, aspire confidently and engage with the wider world.
We celebrate our local community and heritage while ensuring pupils develop a deep understanding of their role within an increasingly diverse and interconnected society. Significant individuals – from local, national and international contexts – are thoughtfully woven throughout our curriculum so that children see themselves and others represented. In doing so, we promote inclusion, empathy and respect, helping pupils understand both their own identity and the perspectives of others.
Our sequential curriculum is coherently planned to ensure that knowledge builds cumulatively over time. Substantive and disciplinary knowledge lie at the heart of each subject, with carefully designed links across areas of learning to strengthen understanding and support long-term retention. We are proud of our collective, evidence-informed practice and our shared pedagogy, which reflects our belief that learning is a lifelong pursuit.
We recognise that memory is fundamental to learning. Therefore, we strategically plan opportunities for pupils to revisit, retrieve and apply prior knowledge, enabling them to think deeply and make meaningful connections. By building on what they already know, children develop broader understanding, deeper knowledge and the confidence to become thoughtful, responsible decision makers.
These drivers help every child grow in confidence, character, and compassion—ready to soar in all they do.
At Beechcroft St Paul’s, all class teachers are responsible for providing a curriculum that is suitable for all pupils in the class, including those with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) with support from the Inclusion Lead. We have high expectations for all pupils and are committed to ensuring our curriculum complies with the Equality Act 2010 and the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014. Our SEND Information Report emphasises the importance of providing an inclusive learning environment for all pupils including those with SEND. Additional information on this can be found in our SEND Policy and on the SEND section of our website. For any parents with queries regarding SEND provision, contact should be made in the first instance with Miss Stuart, Inclusion Lead, via the school office: (01305) 783500 or office@beechcroft.dsat.org.uk
Should you wish for any further information regarding the curriculum, please contact your child's class teacher in the first instance or contact the school office on (01305) 783500 or: office@beechcroft.dsat.org.uk
